Suspected armed bandits have attacked Mbatian community in Dyom, as well as Atuluku, Tse Kasua and Amachigh villages in Ukum Local Government Area of Benue State. The military reportedly responded swiftly, rescuing two abducted women. According to a community source, the attacks occurred between Friday night and Saturday morning. The resident said, “The attack occurred Friday night and Saturday morning. They also attacked military personnel at their duty posts, but luckily, the military repelled them. “The two women were kidnapped by the armed men in Mbatian community but were eventually rescued by the military, who intervened quickly to avert a major disaster in the affected communities,” the source said. Add us to your Preferred Sources Confirming the incident, the Chairman of Ukum LGA, Jonathan Modi, commended officers and men of the Nigerian Army operating in the area for their gallantry, swift response and commitment to protecting lives and property. The chairman, in a statement released by his Special Assistant on Media and Public Communications, Samuel Atsua, said the commendation followed the successful repulsion of the attempted attack on Mbatian community in Dyom and subsequent attacks on other villages. The statement read in part, “The prompt intervention of the Nigerian Army was instrumental in preventing what could have resulted in a devastating loss of lives and destruction of property. Particularly commendable was the rescue of two women reportedly abducted by the suspected attackers from the affected communities.” Fire razes Plateau school, residents suspect bandits Benue APC crisis: Alia, Akume attend peace meeting in Abuja 2027: Outrage over widespread billboard attacks The chairman described the military’s intervention as a demonstration of courage, professionalism and dedication to national service, adding that the presence and operational commitment of security personnel remained critical to restoring confidence among residents and protecting vulnerable communities. In the statement, Modi said he visited the military base at Dyom, where he met with the Commander of the newly established 11 Brigade, Gboko, Brigadier General Akinkunmi Odubiyi, and other personnel. He said, “I assure the Nigerian Army that the Ukum Local Government administration remains committed to providing the necessary support and cooperation to strengthen security operations and ensure the protection of lives, property and territorial integrity of the area.” The chairman urged the military and other security agencies not to relent in their efforts, “particularly in sustaining their presence and responding promptly to security threats across vulnerable communities.” Efforts to get a reaction from the spokesperson for the state police command, DSP Peter Aondongu, were unsuccessful as of the time of filling this report. John Charles
